title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-1ror: Fragment::from_bytes signature changed but test/fuzz callers not updated
description:
## Issue

Commit 0309a17 changed `Fragment::from_bytes` signature from 2-argument (`data, tile`) to 1-argument (`data`), removing the tile buffer parameter. The internal implementation now slices into `data` directly instead of copying into a tile.

However, 6 call sites in test and fuzz files still call the old 2-argument signature and will fail to compile:

- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation_vectors.rs:214` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&wire, &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation_vectors.rs:241` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&wire, &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation_vectors.rs:379` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&wire, &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation.rs:123` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&[...], &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation.rs:125` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&regular_nonzero_padding, &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/tests/fragmentation.rs:236` — `Fragment::from_bytes(&wire[..length], &mut tile)`
- `rust/lichen-schc/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_fragment.rs:8` — `Fragment::from_bytes(data, &mut tile)`

## Additionally

The `write_to` (encode) function was changed from bit-shifting encoding to direct `copy_from_slice`. If tests expected the old bit-shifted wire format, they will also fail. The encode/decode round-trip is now identity (correct), but existing test expectations may be stale.

## Fix needed

1. Update all callers to use the new 1-argument `from_bytes` signature
2. Update test expectations for the `write_to` output if they expected old bit-shifted format
3. Verify full test suite passes
